target: Semakin lama saya tinggal di sini, semakin saya suka kota ini.
english: The longer I live here, the more I like this city.
grammar: Semakin ... semakin = the more ... the more: semakin lama, semakin suka = the longer, the more (I) like it.

target: Semakin mahal restorannya, semakin kecil porsinya.
english: The more expensive the restaurant, the smaller the portions.

target: Harga rumah di daerah ini semakin tinggi setiap tahun.
english: House prices in this area get higher and higher every year.
grammar: Semakin + adjective alone = getting more and more X: semakin tinggi = higher and higher.

target: Semakin sering kamu berlatih, semakin cepat kamu maju.
english: The more often you practice, the faster you improve.

target: Cuaca semakin panas menjelang akhir musim kemarau.
english: The weather gets hotter and hotter toward the end of the dry season.
grammar: Menjelang = approaching (a time): menjelang akhir musim = toward the end of the season.

target: Semakin tua, ayah saya semakin rajin berolahraga.
english: The older he gets, the more diligently my father exercises.

target: Jalan ke pusat kota semakin macet sejak pasar baru dibuka.
english: The road to the city center has gotten more and more congested since the new market opened.

target: Semakin banyak saya membaca tentang pulau itu, semakin ingin saya ke sana.
english: The more I read about that island, the more I want to go there.

target: Antrean di kasir semakin panjang menjelang jam makan siang.
english: The line at the checkout gets longer and longer toward lunchtime.

target: Semakin dekat hari keberangkatan, semakin gugup saya.
english: The closer the departure day gets, the more nervous I am.
grammar: Ke-...-an makes a noun: berangkat = to depart, keberangkatan = departure.

target: Kopi di kafe itu semakin enak setelah mereka mengganti mesinnya.
english: The coffee at that cafe has gotten even better since they replaced the machine.

target: Semakin malam, pasar malam itu semakin ramai.
english: The later it gets at night, the busier that night market becomes.

target: Semakin besar layar ponsel, semakin cepat baterainya habis.
english: The bigger a phone's screen, the faster its battery runs out.

target: Udara di gunung semakin dingin begitu hari mulai gelap.
english: The air in the mountains gets colder and colder once it starts to get dark.

target: Semakin sering dia begadang, semakin sering dia sakit kepala.
english: The more often he stays up late, the more often he gets headaches.
grammar: Begadang = to stay up very late: sering begadang = often stays up late.

target: Sungai di belakang kompleks semakin bersih sejak warga rajin membuang sampah pada tempatnya.
english: The river behind the housing complex has gotten cleaner since residents diligently throw trash where it belongs.

target: Makin siang, jalanan di kota ini makin panas.
english: The later in the day it gets, the hotter the streets in this city are.
grammar: Makin is the everyday spoken short form of semakin: makin siang = the later in the day.

target: Belanja online makin populer, jadi toko kecil harus ikut berjualan di internet.
english: Online shopping is getting more and more popular, so small shops have to start selling on the internet too.

target: Tas ini sama mahalnya dengan tas yang kamu beli kemarin.
english: This bag is as expensive as the bag you bought yesterday.
grammar: Sama + adjective + -nya + dengan = as ... as: sama mahalnya dengan = as expensive as.

target: Kopi di warung ini sama enaknya dengan kopi di kafe mahal.
english: The coffee at this food stall is as good as the coffee at an expensive cafe.

target: Kamar hotel ini sama luasnya dengan kamar tidur saya di rumah.
english: This hotel room is as spacious as my bedroom at home.

target: Adik saya sekarang sama tingginya dengan ayah kami.
english: My younger sibling is now as tall as our father.

target: Harga tiket kereta sama dengan harga tiket bus untuk rute ini.
english: The price of a train ticket is the same as the price of a bus ticket for this route.
grammar: Sama dengan = the same as: harga A sama dengan harga B = price A equals price B.

target: Jadwal kerja saya minggu ini sama dengan jadwal minggu lalu.
english: My work schedule this week is the same as last week's schedule.

target: Berat ponsel baru ini hampir sama dengan ponsel lama saya.
english: This new phone's weight is almost the same as my old phone's.

target: Kebiasaan makan kakak sama dengan kebiasaan ayah; dua-duanya suka pedas.
english: My older sibling's eating habits are the same as father's; they both like spicy food.
grammar: Dua-duanya = both of them: dua-duanya suka pedas = they both like spicy food.

target: Musim hujan tahun ini sama basahnya dengan musim hujan tahun lalu.
english: This year's rainy season is as wet as last year's rainy season.

target: Warna jaket saya sama dengan warna jaket teman sekantor saya.
english: The color of my jacket is the same as the color of my officemate's jacket.

target: Suasana desa ini sama tenangnya dengan desa tempat saya lahir.
english: The atmosphere of this village is as peaceful as the village where I was born.
grammar: Tempat + clause = where: desa tempat saya lahir = the village where I was born.

target: Gaji di kantor baru itu hampir sama dengan gaji saya sekarang.
english: The salary at that new office is almost the same as my current salary.

target: Menu sarapan di dua hotel itu hampir sama.
english: The breakfast menus at those two hotels are almost the same.

target: Laptop ini sama cepatnya dengan laptop kantor, tetapi jauh lebih murah.
english: This laptop is as fast as the office laptop, but much cheaper.
grammar: Jauh lebih = much more: jauh lebih murah = much cheaper.

target: Suara anak kembar itu sama persis; saya sering salah memanggil nama.
english: Those twins' voices are exactly the same; I often call the wrong name.
grammar: Persis = exactly: sama persis = exactly the same.

target: Iklim di Bandung berbeda dengan iklim di Jakarta; di sana jauh lebih sejuk.
english: The climate in Bandung is different from the climate in Jakarta; it is much cooler there.
grammar: Berbeda dengan = different from: berbeda dengan iklim Jakarta = different from Jakarta's climate.

target: Kebiasaan sarapan orang sini berbeda dengan kebiasaan di kampung saya.
english: The breakfast habits of people here are different from the habits back in my hometown.

target: Rasa mangga muda berbeda jauh dengan rasa mangga yang sudah matang.
english: The taste of an unripe mango is very different from the taste of a ripe one.
grammar: Muda usually means young, but for fruit it means unripe: mangga muda = unripe mango.

target: Model tahun ini sedikit berbeda dengan model tahun lalu, tetapi harganya naik jauh.
english: This year's model is slightly different from last year's model, but the price went up a lot.

target: Suasana pasar tradisional berbeda sekali dengan suasana mal yang sejuk.
english: The atmosphere of a traditional market is very different from the atmosphere of a cool mall.

target: Cara adik saya belajar berbeda dengan cara saya; dia harus sambil mendengarkan musik.
english: The way my younger sibling studies is different from my way; he has to listen to music while doing it.

target: Jadwal bus hari Minggu berbeda dengan jadwal hari kerja, jadi cek dulu.
english: The Sunday bus schedule is different from the weekday schedule, so check first.

target: Pendapat saya berbeda dengan pendapat atasan, tetapi kami tetap bekerja sama.
english: My opinion is different from my boss's opinion, but we still work together.

target: Gaya hidup di kota besar jelas berbeda dengan gaya hidup di desa.
english: The lifestyle in a big city is clearly different from the lifestyle in a village.

target: Kopi robusta beda jauh dengan arabika; rasanya lebih pahit dan lebih kuat.
english: Robusta coffee is very different from arabica; it tastes more bitter and stronger.
grammar: Beda is the everyday short form of berbeda: beda jauh = very different.

target: Musim di Indonesia berbeda dengan musim di Eropa; di sini hanya ada dua.
english: The seasons in Indonesia are different from the seasons in Europe; here there are only two.

target: Harga di menu berbeda dengan harga yang saya bayar di kasir.
english: The price on the menu is different from the price I paid at the register.

target: Wajah anak itu mirip sekali dengan wajah ibunya.
english: That child's face looks very much like his mother's face.
grammar: Mirip (dengan) = similar to, looks like: mirip ibunya = looks like his mother.

target: Logo merek baru itu mirip dengan logo merek terkenal, jadi banyak orang bingung.
english: That new brand's logo is similar to a famous brand's logo, so many people are confused.

target: Rasa buah ini mirip mangga, tetapi sedikit lebih asam.
english: This fruit tastes similar to mango, but is slightly more sour.

target: Suara penyanyi muda itu mirip dengan suara penyanyi favorit ayah saya.
english: That young singer's voice is similar to the voice of my father's favorite singer.

target: Kota tua di sini mirip dengan kota tua di Semarang.
english: The old town here is similar to the old town in Semarang.

target: Kebiasaan tidur saya mirip dengan kebiasaan kakek: tidur cepat, bangun sebelum subuh.
english: My sleeping habits are similar to grandfather's habits: sleep early, wake up before dawn.
grammar: Subuh = dawn, the hours before sunrise: bangun sebelum subuh = up before dawn.

target: Desain ponsel ini mirip dengan merek sebelah, tetapi kameranya kalah jauh.
english: This phone's design is similar to the neighboring brand's, but its camera is far behind.
grammar: Kalah jauh = far behind (literally loses by far): kameranya kalah jauh = its camera is far worse.

target: Bau sabun ini mirip bau jeruk segar.
english: This soap's smell is similar to the smell of fresh oranges.

target: Cara dia menjelaskan mirip dengan cara dosen kami mengajar di kelas.
english: The way he explains things is similar to the way our lecturer teaches in class.

target: Rumah-rumah di kompleks ini mirip semua; saya pernah salah masuk pagar.
english: The houses in this complex all look alike; I once went through the wrong gate.

target: Setelah hujan, jalan kampung itu licin seperti kaca.
english: After the rain, that village road is slippery like glass.
grammar: Seperti = like, for comparisons: licin seperti kaca = slippery like glass.

target: Kamar anak saya berantakan seperti kapal pecah.
english: My child's room is a mess, like a broken ship.
grammar: Seperti kapal pecah (like a wrecked ship) is THE image for a hopelessly messy room.

target: Suara mesin cuci tua itu seperti suara pesawat di bandara.
english: The sound of that old washing machine is like the sound of a plane at the airport.

target: Kulit bayi itu halus seperti sutra.
english: That baby's skin is smooth like silk.

target: Antrean tiket konser itu panjang seperti ular.
english: The line for those concert tickets is long like a snake.

target: Siang ini panasnya seperti di dalam oven.
english: This afternoon the heat is like being inside an oven.
grammar: Adding -nya makes hot into the heat: panas = hot, panasnya = the heat.

target: Dia tahu semua gang di kota ini seperti sopir taksi lama.
english: He knows every alley in this city like a longtime taxi driver.

target: Air laut di pantai itu jernih seperti kolam renang.
english: The seawater at that beach is clear like a swimming pool.

target: Kayak mimpi rasanya; tiket promo ke Jepang itu akhirnya saya dapat.
english: It feels like a dream; I finally got that promo ticket to Japan.
grammar: Kayak = colloquial seperti (like); you hear it everywhere: kayak mimpi = like a dream.

target: Kopi buatan ibu pahitnya kayak obat, tetapi saya tetap minum.
english: Mom's coffee is as bitter as medicine, but I drink it anyway.
grammar: Kayak is casual speech; in writing use seperti: pahit kayak obat = bitter like medicine.

target: Setelah lembur seminggu penuh, badan saya lemas seperti tanpa tenaga.
english: After a full week of overtime, my body feels weak, as if it has no energy.

target: Adik tidur nyenyak seperti bayi meskipun tetangga sedang pesta.
english: My younger sibling sleeps soundly like a baby even though the neighbors are having a party.

target: Pagi ini kabut tebal seperti asap; ujung jalan hampir tidak kelihatan.
english: This morning the fog is thick like smoke; the end of the street is barely visible.
grammar: Kelihatan = visible, can be seen: hampir tidak kelihatan = barely visible.

target: Dua sahabat itu selalu pergi bersama seperti perangko dan amplop.
english: Those two best friends always go together, like a stamp and an envelope.

target: Seperti orang baru gajian, dia mentraktir semua teman kantornya.
english: Like someone who just got paid, he treated all his officemates.
grammar: Gajian = payday, having just been paid: baru gajian = fresh off payday.

target: Ini bakso paling enak yang pernah saya coba di kota ini.
english: This is the tastiest bakso I have ever tried in this city.
grammar: Paling + yang pernah = the most ... ever: paling enak yang pernah saya coba = tastiest I ever tried.

target: Gunung itu tempat paling indah yang pernah kami daki.
english: That mountain is the most beautiful place we have ever climbed.

target: Kereta pagi adalah cara paling cepat untuk sampai ke bandara.
english: The morning train is the fastest way to get to the airport.
grammar: Adalah links two nouns (A is B); never use it before an adjective.

target: Februari biasanya bulan paling basah di kota kami.
english: February is usually the wettest month in our city.

target: Kasur ini paling empuk dari semua kasur yang kami coba di toko.
english: This mattress is the softest of all the mattresses we tried in the store.
grammar: Paling ... dari semua = the most ... of all: paling empuk dari semua kasur = softest of all the mattresses.

target: Dia orang paling sabar yang pernah saya kenal di kantor.
english: He is the most patient person I have ever known at the office.

target: Film itu film paling lucu yang kami tonton tahun ini.
english: That movie is the funniest film we watched this year.

target: Sejak dibuka, jalan tol baru menjadi rute paling cepat menuju pelabuhan.
english: Since it opened, the new toll road has become the fastest route to the harbor.

target: Kamar di lantai atas paling sejuk karena dapat angin dari laut.
english: The room upstairs is the coolest because it gets the breeze from the sea.

target: Ini keputusan paling sulit yang pernah saya ambil selama bekerja.
english: This is the hardest decision I have ever made while working.

target: Pantai di sisi timur pulau itu paling sepi pada hari kerja.
english: The beach on the east side of the island is the quietest on weekdays.

target: Nenek selalu bangun paling pagi di rumah kami.
english: Grandma always gets up the earliest in our house.
grammar: Paling also works with time words: bangun paling pagi = up the earliest.

target: Harga di toko itu paling murah, tetapi antreannya juga paling panjang.
english: The prices at that store are the cheapest, but its line is also the longest.
grammar: Ter- + adjective can replace paling: termurah = paling murah = the cheapest.

target: Agustus bulan paling ramai di pulau itu karena musim liburan.
english: August is the busiest month on that island because of the holiday season.

target: Soto di warung ini paling terkenal; turis pun rela antre satu jam.
english: The soto at this stall is the most famous; even tourists are willing to line up for an hour.
grammar: Pun after a noun = even: turis pun = even tourists.

target: Kamus ini paling lengkap untuk pelajar pemula seperti saya.
english: This dictionary is the most complete for beginner learners like me.

target: Dari semua sepatu lari yang saya punya, sepatu ini paling ringan.
english: Of all the running shoes I own, these shoes are the lightest.

target: Menurut hampir semua siswa, ujian hari terakhir paling susah.
english: According to almost all the students, the last day's exam was the hardest.
grammar: Menurut = according to: menurut siswa = according to the students.

target: Lagu itu paling sering diputar di radio sepanjang bulan ini.
english: That song has been played the most often on the radio all this month.

target: Musim kemarau tahun ini paling panjang dalam sepuluh tahun terakhir.
english: This year's dry season is the longest in the last ten years.

target: Saya kira restoran itu mahal, ternyata harganya cukup masuk akal.
english: I thought that restaurant was expensive; it turns out the prices are quite reasonable.
grammar: Ternyata = it turns out: saya kira mahal, ternyata murah = I thought it was expensive, turns out it's cheap.

target: Ternyata jalan kecil di belakang pasar lebih cepat daripada jalan utama.
english: It turns out the small road behind the market is faster than the main road.

target: Kami kira hotel itu jauh dari pantai, ternyata hanya lima menit jalan kaki.
english: We thought that hotel was far from the beach; it turns out it is only a five-minute walk.

target: Ternyata tetangga baru kami dokter di rumah sakit tempat ibu dirawat.
english: It turns out our new neighbor is a doctor at the hospital where mother is being treated.

target: Ponsel murah ini ternyata lebih awet daripada ponsel mahal saya yang dulu.
english: This cheap phone turns out to be more durable than my old expensive phone.
grammar: Awet = long-lasting, durable: lebih awet = lasts longer.

target: Setelah dicoba, resep nenek ternyata lebih enak daripada resep dari internet.
english: After trying it, grandma's recipe turns out to be tastier than the recipe from the internet.

target: Ternyata dia sudah pindah ke Surabaya sejak awal tahun lalu.
english: It turns out he already moved to Surabaya at the beginning of last year.

target: Paket yang saya tunggu seminggu ternyata tertinggal di kantor pos.
english: The package I waited a week for turned out to have been left behind at the post office.
grammar: Tertinggal = left behind by accident: paket ternyata tertinggal = the package got left behind.

target: Ternyata musim kemarau di daerah ini tetap sering hujan pada sore hari.
english: It turns out that in this area's dry season it still often rains in the afternoon.

target: Barang diskon itu ternyata stok lama, jadi saya batal membelinya.
english: That discounted item turned out to be old stock, so I ended up not buying it.

target: Saya pikir dia marah kepada saya, ternyata dia hanya lelah setelah lembur.
english: I thought he was angry at me; it turns out he was just tired after working overtime.

target: Ternyata kunci mobil ada di kantong jaket saya sejak tadi.
english: It turns out the car keys have been in my jacket pocket this whole time.
grammar: Sejak tadi = since earlier, all along: ada di sini sejak tadi = has been here all along.

target: Dia tetap memakai jaket tebal, padahal cuaca hari ini panas sekali.
english: He still wears a thick jacket, even though the weather today is very hot.
grammar: Padahal = even though / when in fact, for surprising contrast: padahal panas = even though it's hot.

target: Adik membeli ponsel baru lagi, padahal ponsel lamanya masih bagus.
english: My younger sibling bought a new phone again, even though his old phone is still fine.

target: Restoran itu selalu penuh, padahal menurut saya rasanya biasa saja.
english: That restaurant is always full, even though in my opinion the food tastes just average.

target: Dia berangkat tanpa payung, padahal langit sudah gelap sejak pagi.
english: He left without an umbrella, even though the sky had been dark since morning.

target: Harga kamar di situ mahal, padahal fasilitasnya sama dengan hotel sebelah.
english: The room rates there are expensive, even though the facilities are the same as the hotel next door.

target: Ayah masih menonton bola sampai larut, padahal besok dia harus bangun jam lima.
english: Father is still watching football until late, even though tomorrow he has to get up at five.

target: Saya lupa membawa dompet, padahal tas sudah saya cek dua kali.
english: I forgot to bring my wallet, even though I had already checked my bag twice.

target: Kota ini terasa sepi, padahal ini malam Minggu.
english: This city feels quiet, even though it is Saturday night.

target: Dia bilang sedang sibuk, padahal saya melihat dia duduk santai di kafe.
english: He says he is busy, even though I saw him sitting relaxed at a cafe.

target: Buah di pasar pagi lebih segar, padahal harganya lebih murah daripada di supermarket.
english: The fruit at the morning market is fresher, even though it costs less than at the supermarket.

target: Anak itu bilang sudah kenyang, padahal makanannya baru habis setengah.
english: That child says he is already full, even though only half of his food is finished.

target: Kami hampir membatalkan piknik, padahal sore itu cuaca akhirnya cerah.
english: We almost canceled the picnic, even though that afternoon the weather turned out sunny.

target: Saya kira dia akan marah, justru dia tertawa mendengar cerita itu.
english: I thought he would be angry; on the contrary, he laughed hearing that story.
grammar: Justru = actually / on the contrary, flips an expectation: justru dia tertawa = on the contrary, he laughed.

target: Obat warung itu justru membuat kepala saya semakin pusing.
english: That corner-store medicine actually made my head even dizzier.

target: Jangan berangkat siang; justru pagi-pagi jalanan lebih kosong.
english: Do not leave at midday; it is actually early in the morning that the roads are emptier.
grammar: Doubling a time word = really early/late: pagi-pagi = early in the morning.

target: Musim hujan justru waktu terbaik untuk menikmati kopi hangat di rumah.
english: The rainy season is actually the best time to enjoy warm coffee at home.

target: Barang yang lebih mahal itu justru rusak lebih dulu.
english: The more expensive item actually broke first.

target: Dia justru lebih tenang setelah mendengar hasil ujian itu.
english: He was actually calmer after hearing that exam result.

target: Di desa kecil itu, sinyal internet justru paling kuat di dekat sawah.
english: In that small village, the internet signal is actually strongest near the rice fields.

target: Saya justru suka rumah tua ini karena halamannya luas.
english: I actually like this old house because its yard is spacious.

target: Kritik dari pelanggan justru membantu toko kami maju.
english: Criticism from customers actually helps our store move forward.

target: Setelah pindah ke kota kecil, pengeluaran kami justru naik.
english: After moving to a small town, our expenses actually went up.

target: Hujan deras semalam justru membuat udara pagi ini segar sekali.
english: Last night's heavy rain actually made this morning's air very fresh.
